This is a review for “Call of Cthulhu.” I played it on PS4. I obtained my copy at a local second hand shop. I thought it would be an interesting game.

I’ve done a couple reviews around here. The first thing to get out of the way is the pozz. In this game there is only a little bit. One strong female character is the bootlegger for the island. There is not multiculturalism or forced diversity otherwise.

You play as a ex war vet from WWI. He was a member of the Lost Battalion. Your character is an alcoholic suffering from nightmares. The occupation he holds is as a P.I. Your character is approached and tasked with uncovering a strange murder on a New England island near Boston.

The gameplay is a mix of Mass Effect, with enough points into your character traits like, investigation, occult, medicine, strength, spot hidden and psychology can unlock different results for play throughs. Character Points are awarded during different times in the game though altering occult and medicine can only be done in the very beginning of the game. Later you can enchance these by finding in game items like medical and occult books. The game is set in first person and you are allowed free roam in a rather linear amount of set pieces. The game has added film grain that can make distinguishing objects a bit difficult and hides technical flaws. The load times are atrocious. You can make a drink or use the bathroom and be back before the loading is done. The frame rate stutters also. This isn’t a graphic intensive game it seems just lower effort development. You interact with characters to gain knowledge of the crime and cursory characters who become important later. You will also interact with your environment to gain knowledge and possibly open up more lines of dialogues with NPCs. There are scenes that remind me of CSI or something where you investigate the scene looking for clues. This is usually where your CP comes into play. Some interactions will be skill based and manual saving is not an option. As you uncover the truth madness in your character will set in. This is similar to Eternal Darkness. Should you drink or choose certain actions your end result will be different. This also makes the game a decent choose your own. However it is canned to five endings.

The story itself is good and has plenty of scary bits. There’s something awful stirring on the island but is it the doctors, a mythological evil or a true event? Shades of Resident Evil permeate some of the scenes and motivations. I personally didn’t expect the outcome that the game led to.

Overall I would say a solid game. Priced around $20 is reasonable for the experience and technical flaws. Multiple endings but you will have to trudge through recycled dialogue and character animations. Creepy and atmospheric a good game for a dark night.
